evidence.quote: we begin with firms making annual capex forecasts (as covered by IBES) and match these firms to Compustat using the IBES link file.
This gives us an initial sample of 40,785 forecasts between the years 2002 and 2016 (where year denotes the year of the forecast).
Matching these forecasts with CRSP to obtain short-window market reaction (on the issuance date) reduces the sample to 36,900 forecasts.
We delete 17,473 forecasts that are made concurrently with an earnings forecast and another 1,850 that are made in 2016 because we need actual capital expenditure data as of the end of the year.
Our unit of observation in most tables is a firm-quarter.

items.label: Dependent variable
items.value: CAPEX_ADJ: percentage deviation of actual capex from forecasted capex scaled by the latter

evidence.quote: The dependent variable is capex adjustments (CAPEX_ADJ) defined as the percentage deviation of actual capex from forecasted capex scaled by the latter.

items.label: Key independent variable(s)
value: CAR: cumulative abnormal returns around the forecast date, standardized to zero mean and unit standard deviation
SF_CAR: market reaction to sales forecasts made for the same fiscal period and closest to the capex forecast, standardized to zero mean and unit standard deviation
MKTRET: market returns on the forecast date, standardized to zero mean and unit standard deviation
CAR_PRE: pseudo-market reactions around a nonforecast date, standardized to zero mean and unit standard deviation

evidence.quote: CAR denotes cumulative abnormal returns around the forecast date.
SF_CAR denotes market reaction to sales forecasts made for the same fiscal period and closest to the capex forecast.
MKTRET denotes market returns on the forecast date.
CAR_PRE denotes pseudo-market reactions around a nonforecast date.
CAR, SF_CAR, MKTRET, and CAR_PRE have been standardized to have zero means and unit standard deviations.

items.label: Control variables
value: SIZE: firm size defined as the log of market value of equity (closing stock price times shares outstanding), calculated as of the end of the quarter preceding the capex forecast quarter
LAG_CAPX: most recent year's annual capex scaled by start of year market value
SURP: earnings surprise for the most recent quarter defined as the quarter's earnings-per-share minus that of the same quarter of the previous year
EA_DUM: indicator to denote capex announcements accompanied by earnings announcements

evidence.quote: SIZE denotes firm size defined as the log of market value of equity (closing stock price times shares outstanding) and is calculated as of the end of the quarter preceding the capex forecast quarter.
LAG_CAPX denotes the most recent year's annual capex scaled by start of year market value.
SURP denotes earnings surprise for the most recent quarter defined as the quarter's earnings-per-share minus that of the same quarter of the previous year.
EA_DUM is an indicator to denote capex announcements accompanied by earnings announcements.
Model 3 includes year-quarter fixed effects, whereas Models 4 to 8 include firm and year-quarter fixed effects.

items.label: Subsamples / column structure
items.value: Models differ by specification: Model 1 univariate; Model 2 adds SIZE; Model 3 adds year-quarter fixed effects; Model 4 adds firm and year-quarter fixed effects; Model 5 clusters by industry; Model 6 adds SF_CAR and uses the 3,456-forecast subsample with corresponding sales forecasts; Model 7 adds MKTRET and CAR_PRE; Model 8 adds LAG_CAPX, SURP, EA_DUM.

evidence.quote: Model 1 presents univariate evidence where CAPEX_ADJ is regressed on CAR without controlling for SIZE or the fixed effects.

The above result is robust to controlling for firm size (Model 2), including time fixed effects (Model 3), firm and time fixed effects (Model 4), and to clustering by industry rather than by firm (Model 5).
Model 6 presents results of a falsification test where we include the market reaction to managerial sales forecasts (SF_CAR).
These inferences are based on a smaller sample of 3,456 capex forecasts for which we can find a corresponding sales forecast made by the firm for the same fiscal period.

Model 7 presents results of two other falsification tests, where we include the aggregate market returns measured using the S&P 500 index (MKTRET) on the capex forecast date, as well as a pseudo-market reaction variable (CAR_PRE)
Finally, Model 8 includes additional controls in the specification.
